label: parse-csv-python-pandas-en
top_ai_sentences: Pick the tool that fits the file size and the operations you need.

| Approach | Library | Memory | Use When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DictReader | csv (stdlib) | Low | Simple row iteration |
| pandas read_csv | pandas | High | Filtering, group

When a CSV is larger than 500MB, set chunksize to
keep memory usage under control.
Check memory usage by calling df.memory_usage(deep=True).

Don't treat an Excel spreadsheet as a CSV
file; open spreadsheets with a dedicated reader
instead of parsing them as CSV.

The read_csv function takes parameters for the delimiter (sep), the file
encoding, the column types (dtype), date parsing, custom null values, and
which columns to load (usecols).

Before parsing the whole file, look at the headers, the row count, and the file
size.

When you need
filtering, grouping, joins, or large-file handling, use pandas instead.

It also helps
when a file is too big for memory, or when the CSV has weird quoting, mixed
encodings, or unexpected delimiters.

The two functions differ only in the default separator: read_table starts with
a tab, while read_csv starts with a comma.

The csv module reads one row at a time, so it stays lightweight and
memory-efficient.
When a CSV has no header row, set header=None in read_csv.
With pandas, the whole file becomes an in-memory DataFrame.
It's all you need for plain row-by-row iteration.
That keeps memory low and avoids type-inference surprises.

When the
file is larger than RAM, process it in batches with chunksize and set dtype
explicitly.
CSV remains the default format for moving tabular data between systems.
Loading only the columns you actually need keeps memory low.

Switch from
csv.DictReader to csv.reader if you prefer a plain tuple for each row.

On Windows, the csv module adds extra blank rows if the open() call omits the
newline="" argument.

You get vectorized
operations, filtering, grouping, and joins, but memory can grow quickly.

The usecols
argument handles that.

You can avoid silent string-to-NaN conversions by
setting the dtype option explicitly on mixed columns.

For very large DataFrames, look at
Polars or Dask.

For
plain row iteration, Python's built-in csv module is enough.
